title: Cursor update on packed words
statement: Let $M$ be a Turing machine with a finite state set and Boolean tape alphabet, let $C,e,c,A,d$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a finite bit string, and let $i$ be a natural number. Set $T=c\bigl(A(|x|+C(|x|+1)^e+1)^d+1\bigr)^2$ and $R=|x|+(M.k+3)T+M.k+1$, where $M.k$ is the number of work tapes of $M$. If $i\le R+1$, then applying the cursor update to the packed encoding with unary cursor $i$ and data determined by $M,C,e,c,A,d,x$ yields the packed encoding with the same data and unary cursor $\min(i+1,R+1)$; in particular, the cursor remains at $R+1$ once it reaches that value.
hypotheses_covered: A Turing machine with a finite state set and Boolean tape alphabet
The bound $i\le R+1$, with $T$ and $R$ as stated
replaced: For every source machine, parameters, instance $x$, and cursor $i$ at most the last round plus one, the native cursor update of the body word at $i$ is the body word at $\min(i+1, R+1)$, where $R$ is the last round; the saturated cursor is stationary.
